title: Fixed Deposits: Understanding Tax on FD Interest in India
description: Interest earned on regular Fixed Deposits (FDs) is fully taxable as 'Income from Other Sources' under Indian tax law. This interest income is added to your to.

faq.q: ### Is FD interest fully tax-free if I submit Form 15G/15H?
faq.a: No, submitting Form 15G/15H only prevents the bank from deducting TDS. The interest earned is still considered taxable income and must be declared in your income tax return. You will pay tax on it if your total income exceeds the basic exemption limit.

faq.q: ### What happens if I don't provide PAN to the bank for my FD?
faq.a: If you do not provide your PAN, the bank will deduct TDS at a higher rate of 20% on your FD interest, instead of the standard 10%, once the threshold is crossed. This can result in a larger upfront tax deduction.

faq.q: ### Is interest from tax-saving FDs also taxable?
faq.a: Yes, while the principal amount invested in a tax-saving FD qualifies for deduction under Section 80C, the interest earned on it is fully taxable as per your income tax slab.

faq.q: ### Can NRIs save tax on FD interest in India?
faq.a: NRIs are subject to TDS on FD interest at a rate of 30% (plus surcharge and cess) in India. However, they may be able to claim tax relief under Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAA) between India and their country of residence.

faq.q: ### Do all banks deduct TDS on FD interest?
faq.a: Yes, all banks and financial institutions offering Fixed Deposits are legally mandated to deduct TDS if the interest paid or accrued exceeds the prescribed limit (₹40,000 for regular citizens, ₹50,000 for senior citizens) in a financial year.

faq.q: ### Is there any tax benefit for senior citizens on FD interest?
faq.a: Yes, senior citizens (aged 60 and above) get a higher TDS threshold of ₹50,000 on FD interest. Additionally, they can claim a deduction of up to ₹50,000 on interest income from FDs and savings accounts under Section 80TTB of the Income Tax Act.
